From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Root cause & remediation for ACME token count / duplicate charges (postmortem)

Hi Sam / team — quick summary from our ops investigation:

What happened:
- At 03:08 PDT on 2026-03-18 we deployed a routing change intended to improve regional failover. An unexpected interaction with our batching layer duplicated a small portion of request envelopes for ~32 minutes (03:10–03:42). This caused token accounting to double-count tokens for affected requests and generated duplicate invoice lines for some batched billing records.

Scope:
- Affected account subset: customers routed through the new failover path; Acme was in the cohort.
- Volume impact for ACME: ~2,400 requests affected, ~1.9M tokens double-counted on the 03:10–03:42 window.

What we’ve done:
- Reverted the routing change and disabled the batching optimization that triggered duplication.
- Reconciled the request logs to identify duplicated envelopes. Attached: duplicate_charges_audit.csv (rows: request_id, timestamp, original_tokens, counted_tokens) and a short postmortem PDF with timeline and mitigation steps.
- Generated an adjusted invoice (adjustment-invoice-ACME-0318.pdf) and credited the overcharged amount. The credit equals the duplicated-token unit cost for the affected window.

Proposed remediation & controls:
- Additional pre-deploy smoke tests for batching changes covering edge-case failure modes.
- Alerting on token-count variance exceeding 15% vs 1-hour baseline.
- Weekend canary deploy window to reduce customer blast radius for routing changes.

Next steps for Acme:
- Neha: final billing action below (credit vs adjusted invoice).
- Rachel: coordinate client-facing note and attach official postmortem if they want to share internally.

We sincerely apologize for the operational impact. We know unexpected billing items are disruptive for audits and procurement. We’ll make sure the accounting record is clean and provide the evidence you need for your auditor.

—Marissa
